page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance operates at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. It consists of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench (2258.0) and text processing (2843.0), as well as strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (35.11 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.8 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weaker. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance (3485.37), Passmark CPU score (6350.73), and large-block memory read/write bandwidths (32.39 GB/sec and 20.69 GB/sec respectively) fall into the lower performance tiers.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core, the c4-highmem-4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The presence of advanced instruction sets, such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), supports specialized tasks like low-parameter LLM inference, where it achieves average speeds of 443.85 tokens/sec for 135M model prompt processing. The instance is best suited for single-threaded applications, text processing, light database operations, and memory-bound workloads that can operate within its 4 vCPU limit.
